100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On July 31, 1926, the British government faced escalating tensions as a general strike threatened to paralyze the nation amidst rising labor unrest. Meanwhile, in Germany, Chancellor Wilhelm Marx struggled to stabilize the economy as hyperinflation continued to wreak havoc on the currency. Across the Atlantic, the United States saw ongoing debates over Prohibition, with some states pushing for reforms amidst growing public discontent.
